At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.
Location: Boston, Indianapolis, Louisville, San Francisco, UK, Alcobendas
Reports to: AVP Computational Chemistry & Cheminformatics, Early Molecule Discovery, LSMD
Overview:
At Lilly, we serve an extraordinary purpose. We make a difference for people around the globe by discovering, developing, and delivering medicines that help them live longer, healthier, more active lives.
Lilly Catalyze360 is a comprehensive approach to enabling the early-stage biotech ecosystem by democratizing access to infrastructure, expertise, and resources. Through its interconnected pillars — Lilly Ventures, Lilly Gateway Labs, Lilly ExploR&D, and Lilly TuneLab — Catalyze360 strategically removes barriers that traditionally block bold science from becoming life-changing medicines, providing biotechs with flexible combinations of capital, physical lab space, R&D capabilities, AI/ML tools, and decades of enterprise learning.
Lilly ExploR&D is a team of drug discovery and development experts who partner with biotechs from discovery through clinical proof-of-concept, putting Lilly’s industry-leading capabilities behind their missions. We provide flexible support — from strategic consulting to full program execution — making it faster, easier, and more capital-efficient for innovators to transform bold science into life-changing medicines.
The Lilly Small Molecule Discovery group (LSMD) is an internal research organization dedicated to creating molecules that make life better for people. LSMD applies cutting-edge science to unlock new small-molecule approaches for diseases with limited treatment options.
Both Lilly ExploR&D and LSMD are committed to discovering innovative molecules that deliver breakthrough efficacy with the strongest possible safety margins. Their success in external and internal innovation is grounded in a culture of scientific excellence, open collaboration, creative problem solving, and individual accountability.
Position Summary:
ExploR&D’s Molecule Discovery Team is expanding its capabilities to partner with small-molecule biotechs at any stage of discovery. To support this effort, the team works closely with Lilly’s LSMD organization and draws on its technical expertise in small-molecule hit-to-lead and lead optimization, including the application of state-of-the-art computational chemistry technologies across innovative targets.
We seek an expert computational chemist with a proven record of applying in silico technologies to discover high-quality hit and lead molecules for difficult-to-drug therapeutic targets. This lead-from-the-bench role requires a dynamic, versatile, hands-on scientist who can quickly adapt to each biotech partner and help advance novel targets and therapeutic hypotheses, regardless of the stage or complexity of the discovery campaign.
In close partnership with the LSMD Early Molecular Discovery Computational Chemistry and Cheminformatics team, the ExploR&D Computational Chemist will apply virtual screening, cheminformatics, and AI/ML technologies to support screening library design, hit identification/modelling, and virtual hit expansion toward novel, efficacious lead molecules. The candidate will also conduct advanced generative and structure-based molecular design and fully leverage the TuneLab drug discovery AI/ML platform and its predictive models. This highly collaborative role requires seamless engagement with Lilly cross-functional partners to create data-driven design hypotheses and models while collaborating to accelerate biotech molecule discovery. Success in this position requires excellent interpersonal skills, a positive can-do attitude, and the ability to thrive in a fluid, fast-paced, and highly interactive team environment.
Responsibilities:
• Lead from the bench by applying state-of-the-art computational chemistry, virtual screening, cheminformatics, ML/AI, and advanced analytics to support target, ligand-binding domain, and mechanism-of-action assessments; library design; hit identification; and hit-to-lead progression across multiple target classes and modalities.
• Seamlessly engage with biotech teams, external medicinal chemists, biologists, and other internal and external partners to develop workflows that generate optimal screening collections, high-quality models, and testable ligand-design hypotheses, strengthening the ability of Biotech/ExploR&D collaboration teams to deliver differentiated hits and leads.
• Support joint-team success by guiding the application of modern cheminformatics and ML/AI methods to library design—including diversity, focused, bridging, fragment, and DEL collections—large-data analysis, predictive active-learning models, internal and external data mining, hit prioritization and expansion, and ligand- or fragment-based design.
• Proactively leverage emerging technologies that can accelerate prosecution of challenging targets and delivery of differentiated, high-quality leads.
• Cultivate cross-area collaborations with TuneLab platform colleagues to guide and apply transformative approaches for predictive model development and hit and lead discovery.
• Deliver timely, high-quality data, rigorous analyses, and robust models to joint project teams to accelerate decisions on chemical series and project progression.
• Demonstrate curiosity and learning agility by learning from and adapting to non-small-molecule modalities, such as antibodies and RNA therapeutics, with the medium- to long-term goal of expanding ExploR&D computational chemistry capabilities into these areas.
• Provide strong scientific leadership and strategic guidance across all ExploR&D computational chemistry activities to drive data-driven drug discovery.
Basic Requirements:
• PhD in Computational Chemistry, Cheminformatics, CompBiophysics or a related field, with at least 7 years of relevant research and/or industry experience (may include post-doc experience), or MS with 10+ years industry/academic/research, or BS with 15+ years industry/academic/research experience.
• Exceptional record of applying computational chemistry, virtual screening, and cheminformatics approaches to accelerate target assessment, hit identification and expansion, lead generation, and library design as exemplified through patent contributions and high- impact publications.

presentation best practices​

audience-focused visual communication​

JLL empowers you to shape a brighter way.
Our people at JLL are shaping the future of real estate for a better world by combining world class services, advisory and technology for our clients. We are committed to hiring the best, most talented people and empowering them to thrive, grow meaningful careers and to find a place where they belong.  Whether you’ve got deep experience in commercial real estate, skilled trades or technology, or you’re looking to apply your relevant experience to a new industry, join our team as we help shape a brighter way forward.
Global Programme Experience Lead
Location: EMEA
Reporting into: Global Lead, Experience Services
At JLL, our goal is to provide workplace experiences that will be long remembered by our clients. The programmes behind those experiences need to be built once, built well, and deployed consistently across every region and account we serve. This role builds them. It combines programme design, commercial ownership and global enablement, and it suits someone who wants to shape how workplace experience is delivered at scale rather than deliver it account by account.
What this job involves:
As Global Head of Experience Programmes, you will own JLL's global portfolio of workplace experience programmes — designing them, setting the standards they are delivered to, equipping regional and account teams to deploy them, and driving their adoption across 100+ client accounts in 80+ countries, effectively identifying and utilising AI and technology.
This is a build-and-scale role rather than an account delivery role. You will not run accounts. You will define what a programme is for, what good looks like, and how success is measured, then make it work everywhere. Your primary measure of success is adoption: how widely and how faithfully your programmes are deployed, and what they demonstrably produce for clients and for JLL.
The role works largely through influence. You will own the programmes, but the people deploying them will not report to you. Candidates who find that challenge interesting rather than concerning tend to do well in it.
Personal Profile:
I build things that work in more than one place. I design programmes that hold up across sectors, cultures and account types, and I care as much about whether they get used as whether they are well designed. I work through other people's teams rather than my own, which means I earn adoption rather than mandate it. I am commercially minded: I know what a programme costs, what it is worth, and how to prove it. When something is not being taken up, I assume the design is the problem before I assume the region is. New technology and innovation excites me.
What your day-to-day will look like:
Programme Design and Development
• Design global workplace experience programmes that work across sectors, regions and account types, from concept through to deployable product
• Define the purpose, standard and success measures for each programme before it reaches an account
• Build the supporting assets: playbooks, toolkits, templates, training and delivery guidance
• Own the programme lifecycle — refresh, iterate and retire — so the portfolio stays current rather than accumulating
Standards and Quality
• Set the global standards to which experience programmes are delivered, including the minimum viable version for accounts of differing size and maturity
• Establish how consistency is assessed, and work with regional leaders where delivery drifts from standard
• Ensure programmes adapt to local and cultural context without losing what makes them effective
Enablement and Adoption
• Equip regional and account teams to deploy programmes confidently through training, onboarding and ongoing support
• Drive adoption across the global account portfolio — the primary measure of success in this role
• Work through JLL's Experience Leadership community to build capability and surface what is working in the field
• Diagnose the causes of low adoption and address them through design, not through compliance pressure
Commercial Ownership
• Own and be accountable for the commercial structure of the programme portfolio, including tiering, packaging and input to pricing
• Support new business pursuits with programme content and subject matter expertise, and track conversion on pursuits supported
• Make evidence-based investment decisions on which programmes to scale, fix or stop
Measurement and Reporting
• Define the metrics that demonstrate what experience programmes deliver: adoption, employee sentiment, utilisation, retention and commercial contribution
• Work with data and analytics colleagues to build the measurement infrastructure, and use it to inform programme decisions
• Report programme performance and return on investment to JLL leadership, and equip account teams to report to clients
• Manage programme budgets and expenditure in accordance with financial guidelines
Experience and Skills:
• 15+ years in workplace services, facilities management, corporate hospitality or a related field, with significant experience operating globally or across multiple regions
• Track record of building something repeatable — a programme, product, service offering or methodology — and deploying it across multiple sites, markets or business units
• Proven ability to drive adoption without direct authority in a complex matrix organisation
• Strong commercial acumen: how offerings are packaged and priced, and how programme decisions affect account economics
• Demonstrable ability to define and report metrics that evidence business impact rather than activity
• Operational credibility with delivery teams — experience of doing the work, not only designing it
• Excellent communication and presentation skills, including with senior stakeholders
• Proven AI and technology skills
• Fluent in English (both written and verbal)
Preferred:
• Product management, service design or journey mapping methodology
• Working fluency with data and analytics: able to interrogate dashboards, work with analytics teams and translate portfolio data into decisions
• Experience building training or enablement programmes at scale
• Change management experience at organisational scale
• Industry certifications in facility management, hospitality or organisational development

Job Description:
Your impact
Are you ready to launch your career and make an impact on real-world projects from day one?
At Leonardo, we’re looking for graduates who want to be part of something extraordinary - shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.
We are committed to developing our graduates into leading technical or business professionals, and as such we will also support you through your preferred route for professional development.
At Leonardo, we develop the advanced technologies that help keep people safe. As a Graduate Firmware Engineer, you'll join a team delivering world-leading Electronic Warfare capabilities that protect fast jets, UAVs, naval vessels and land platforms operating in some of the world's most demanding environments.
Our structured 18-month Graduate Programme is designed to accelerate your development from graduate to professional engineer. From day one, you'll contribute to real projects, work alongside industry experts, and gain hands-on experience across the full firmware development lifecycle.
This opportunity is based in Luton, with flexible and hybrid working arrangements available. Occasional travel within the UK and overseas may be required to support technical reviews, trials and customer engagements.
What You'll Do
As part of our Firmware Engineering team, you'll support the development of high-performance digital systems used within advanced Electronic Warfare solutions.
Your activities will include:
• Designing and developing FPGA firmware solutions for complex embedded and real-time systems
• Creating and verifying designs using hardware description languages and industry-standard development tools
• Supporting the development of digital processing technologies used in Electronic Warfare and sensing applications
• Conducting simulation, testing and validation activities to ensure firmware meets functional, timing and performance requirements
• Analysing technical data and presenting findings to engineering teams and stakeholders
• Collaborating with multidisciplinary teams across systems, hardware, software and verification engineering to integrate firmware solutions into larger products
• Contributing to technical documentation, design reviews and customer deliverables
• Developing an understanding of the complete engineering lifecycle, from concept through to manufacture and in-service support
What We're Looking For
We're looking for curious, motivated graduates with a passion for engineering, problem solving and technology.
You should have, or be on track to achieve:
• A minimum 2:2 Bachelor's degree, Integrated Master's degree, MSc or PhD in a relevant STEM discipline, such as:
• Electronic Engineering
• Electrical Engineering
• Computer Engineering
• Robotics Engineering
• AI & Cybernetics
• Communications Engineering
• Information Engineering
• Space Engineering
• Physics or Applied Physics
• Mathematics or Applied Mathematics
• Computer Science
• Cyber Security
• Computer Communication and Networks
• Related disciplines
We'd also like to see:
• An interest in firmware development, FPGA design, embedded systems or digital signal processing
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
• The ability to communicate technical concepts clearly and effectively
• A collaborative approach and willingness to learn from experienced engineers
• Experience of programming, simulation, digital design or laboratory-based testing gained through university projects, placements or personal interests (desirable, not essential)
• Familiarity with hardware description languages such as VHDL, Verilog or SystemVerilog, or FPGA development tools, is beneficial but not essential
Our Graduate Programme
Our Graduate Programme has been designed to help you build the skills, knowledge and confidence needed to become a future engineering leader.
You'll benefit from:
• Structured professional development and technical training
• Support from experienced engineers, mentors and the wider graduate community
• Opportunities to work on meaningful projects with real customer impact
• Development towards professional registration, where applicable
• Exposure to a wide range of technologies, products and engineering disciplines
• Networking opportunities across Leonardo's UK business
Security Clearance
Many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations.  As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.

The Role:
Joining Moderna means advancing mRNA science to transform medicine. Work with exceptional global teams on a broad pipeline and build a career that makes a real difference for patients.
This role sits at the forefront of Moderna’s clinical bioanalytical strategy, providing deep scientific expertise and hands-on leadership across immunogenicity and ligand binding assay (LBA) bioanalysis for our mRNA-LNP therapeutic pipeline. As an individual contributor, you will shape and execute phase-appropriate bioanalytical strategies that enable critical clinical development decisions while ensuring the highest standards of scientific rigor and regulatory compliance.
Working closely with cross-functional development teams, you will drive regulated immunogenicity and bioanalytical activities spanning assay development, validation, sample analysis, data interpretation, and regulatory support. You will play a pivotal role in advancing innovative medicines through clinical development while leveraging modern digital capabilities and emerging analytical technologies, including opportunities to work alongside advanced data and AI-enabled approaches that accelerate scientific insight generation.
Here’s What You’ll Do:
• Provide scientific and hands-on oversight of ligand binding assay (LBA)-based bioanalyses supporting Moderna’s mRNA-LNP therapeutic development programs.
• Support and oversee the Immunogenicity function through clinical science-driven, phase-appropriate, and risk-based bioanalytical development strategies across advancing stages of clinical development.
• Lead and facilitate anti-drug antibody (ADA) assay and neutralizing antibody assay regulated method development, validation, and clinical sample testing activities.
• Ensure in-house GcLP compliance across the LBA team, systems, and procedures, maintaining rigorous laboratory practices and regulatory requirements for analytical activities through a phase-appropriate approach.
• Design and execute phase-appropriate clinical analytical strategies supporting development programs.
• Drive development, validation, and implementation of:
• Cell-based assays
• Immunoassays
• Quantitation of translated proteins
• Pharmacokinetic (PK) assays
• Pharmacodynamic (PD) assays
• Review and evaluate raw analytical data, assay validation data, and study reports to ensure scientific integrity, data quality, and compliance with current regulatory, industry, and Moderna standards.
• Assess analytical performance and laboratory compliance to ensure data generated meet both scientific and regulatory expectations.
• Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to support clinical bioanalytical activities throughout the product development lifecycle.
• Contribute to regulatory submissions and support responses to regulatory authority questions and information requests.
• Maintain current knowledge of emerging scientific literature, industry best practices, regulatory expectations, and evolving guidance related to clinical bioanalysis.
• Ensure adherence to Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (GcLP), Good Laboratory Practice (GLP), Good Clinical Practice (GCP), internal SOPs, applicable regulations, guidance documents, and relevant white papers.
• Apply scientific judgment and risk-based decision making to support robust bioanalytical strategies that accelerate development while maintaining quality and compliance.
• Partner with multidisciplinary teams to advance innovative analytical approaches and continuously improve laboratory and bioanalytical processes.
The key Moderna Mindsets you’ll need to succeed in the role:
• We obsess over learning. We don’t have to be the smartest we have to learn the fastest.
• We act with dynamic range, driving strategy and execution at the same time at every step.

• A Ph.D. in infectious disease, Immuno-oncology, Immunology, Cancer Biology, or related fields and a minimum of 10+ years of industry biotech/pharmaceutical experience. M.S. with extensive bioanalytical experience are considered
• Experience with RNA, biologics and cell therapy preferred
• Experience of various platforms such as ECL, Gyrolabs, reporter gene assays, DelPhia assays and other methodologies for clinical assays.
• Ability to effectively communicate scientific concepts, program objectives, data analysis within a matrix environment.
• Knowledge of GLP requirements and understanding of current industry trends and regulatory expectations associated with bioanalytical science.
• Experience on Watson LIMS and LabVnatage eLBN would be an advantage.
• A desire to make an impact as part of a high-growth, transformational companythat is Bold, Relentless, Curious, and Collaborative.

ICON is a global healthcare intelligence and clinical research organisation united by a mission to bring new medicines and treatments to patients faster.
As a values-driven organisation, integrity, collaboration, agility, and inclusion are at the heart of how we work and interact with each other, customers, patients and suppliers.
At ICON, our ability to deliver for customers depends on having the right talent, in the right place, at the right time, across one of the largest and most complex clinical research portfolios in the industry. In this capacity, you will partner directly with the Chief Executive Officer, Executive Leadership Team, Finance, and business presidents to evaluate workforce investments, balance growth ambitions with operational realities, and ensure talent decisions support the company's long-term strategic objectives.
You will lead a high-performing global organization through a team of experienced senior leaders and subject matter experts. The foundation is strong; the opportunity is to elevate the function into a world-class strategic capability. Success will require an executive who can shape enterprise thinking, drive transformational improvement, influence senior leaders across the organization, and establish workforce planning as a competitive advantage for ICON.

Define and lead ICON's global workforce planning and resource management strategy, ensuring talent investments, capacity decisions, and workforce deployment support the organization's growth ambitions, delivery commitments, operational performance, and long-term business objectives.
•
Own the enterprise-wide demand forecasting, capacity planning, resource deployment, and workforce analytics framework, translating commercial forecasts, portfolio dynamics, and business priorities into actionable workforce strategies and executive decision-making insights.
•
Lead ICON's global Headcount Approval Process, establishing governance standards, analytical rigor, and decision frameworks that guide workforce investment decisions across all functions, business units, and geographies.
•
Serve as a trusted advisor to the Chief Executive Officer, Executive Leadership Team, Finance leadership, and business presidents, providing strategic guidance on workforce investments, organizational capacity, delivery risk, productivity, and resource optimization.

Influence critical workforce and organizational decisions by partnering with senior stakeholders to evaluate resource requirements, challenge assumptions, balance competing priorities, and ensure alignment with enterprise objectives, delivery excellence, and financial performance goals.

On joining, you will receive a starting salary of £34,000 per annum, plus a £1,000 welcome bonus. You’ll also be eligible for a £1,000 exit bonus upon successful completion of the programme. In addition, you may be eligible for a Temporary Accommodation Allowance (TAA), subject to specific criteria.
We encourage you to spend at least three days each week on site to integrate with your team and maximise your learning experience.
What you will do as a Graduate Systems Engineer
Luton is the home to around 1,000 people who are involved in the design and development of Leonardo’s Electronic Warfare (EW) capability, which is used to protect airborne platforms from a range of RF-based threats.  This includes:
• The protection systems for current and future RAF and Army aircraft, including Typhoon and Apache.
• The technology development platforms being developed by the UK’s Team Tempest to support the development of a new 6th generation aircraft within the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP).
• Concept demonstrators for future Electronic Warfare technologies and systems.
• Air Platform Protection systems for export customer aircraft.
• Technology to draw insights from the vast amounts of data collected by our electronic surveillance systems using artificial intelligence and machine learning.
Graduate Systems Engineers support the development of world-leading technologies and capabilities across multiple Avionic Systems and Platforms.  As a Graduate Systems Engineer you will have the opportunity to be involved in different phases of the systems engineering lifecycle to create and deliver new and emerging capabilities required by our customers; from understanding the customer’s requirements, developing system architectures and concept designs for the next generation of EW capability, through to live trials of equipment and systems alongside our customers and end-users.
Working as part of an established systems engineering community and supported by a team of experienced engineers, you will be responsible for:
• Developing practical skills in engineering design and development for complex systems, understanding key processes and technologies.
• Gaining an understanding of the EW domain to support the development of relevant products and technologies.
• Working closely with engineers across multiple disciplines to solve problems.
• Completing tasks to a high standard in accordance with appropriate processes and procedures.
• Taking an active role in engineering process improvement, ensuring the communication of best practice across the systems engineering team.
• Developing and applying your academic skills to solve problems, generate ideas and be proactive within the team.
Entry Requirements
All of our roles require (a) a minimum of a 2:2 Bachelors/Integrated Master’s degree, or (b) a higher degree, such as a MSc or PhD.
For the Graduate Systems Engineer role, the acceptable degrees are: aerospace/aeronautical engineering, computer science/systems, electrical/electronic engineering, general engineering, mathematics, mechanical engineering, physics, and systems engineering.
You must have an understanding of mathematics to at least A-Level standard, and a basic understanding of electronics.
You should also ideally have experience of working with engineering development tools (e.g. MATLAB, Simulink, Rhapsody, Cameo, DOORS, a document management system).
Security Clearance
Many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations.  As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.
For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV).  As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.
To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years.  In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks.  Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.

A bit about us
Big responsibility. Personal support. That’s Beyond the Ordinary.
Want to get stuck into client work, build your confidence and start shaping your career from day one? Welcome to the Audit Graduate Programme at BDO.
The programme starts on Monday, 20th September 2027, for an organisation-wide induction (you need to be able to attend).
A bit about Audit
Audit at BDO gives you the chance to take on meaningful work early in your career. We’re the only UK mid-market organisation with more than £1bn in turnover and 8,000 people. That means you get the scale and breadth of a major professional services business, while working with clients where your contribution can make a real difference.
Our Audit teams work across specialist areas including Pension Audit, Public Sector, Not-for-Profit, Financial Services and Technology Risk Assurance, helping deliver high-quality audits that businesses and their stakeholders can trust.
You’ll be trusted with lots of responsibility, but you won’t be expected to figure everything out by yourself. You’ll work alongside experienced colleagues, managers, directors and partners who are there to answer questions, share what they know and help you develop.
It’s a chance to learn by doing, get exposure to clients and build your confidence as your responsibility grows. Big responsibility, with the scale of BDO behind you and personal support around you.
And a bit about the programme
Over three years, you’ll build hands-on experience while working towards a recognised professional qualification with ICAS.
Alongside your studies, you’ll develop your technical and commercial skills through real Audit work. You could gain experience across different clients, sectors and specialist areas, while learning from people across the organisation.
As you develop, so will the responsibility you’re trusted with. Our graduates have talked about joining client calls, leading meetings and working directly with senior colleagues earlier than they expected. You’ll have support around you as you take those next steps and build towards where you want your career to go.
When you successfully complete the programme and pass the exams, you’ll be fully qualified as an accountant, and guaranteed a permanent role with us.
As for you
You’re curious, resilient and adaptable. You’re ready to learn, ask questions and take on more responsibility as you grow.
Bring your problem-solving, analytical skills and critical thinking. We’ll give you opportunities to put them into practice, alongside the support to keep developing.
Join us in one of our hubs in Edinburgh or Glasgow. We have roles in our Financial Services Audit teams and our Audit teams.
One thing to note: you’ll need to live within a commutable distance of the office you apply to. Relocation support is not provided, so please consider this carefully before applying. Time together in person matters – whether that’s in the office or with clients. It gives you more opportunities to learn from your team, build relationships and get the most from working together.
Is it for you? To apply, you’ll need:
• A minimum 2:2 degree in any discipline (obtained or predicted)
• Three A-levels (or equivalent) at A*-C (excluding General Studies and Extended Projects), or four Scottish Highers or Advanced Highers at grade A-B (or equivalent, for example BTEC Extended Diploma). Please note: we do not use UCAS points. You’ll be asked to provide evidence if you’re successful in securing an offer
• GCSEs at grade 4 and above in Maths and English, or Scottish National 5 grade A-C. You’ll also need to provide evidence if successful
• Commitment to balance study and professional work
• The right to work in the UK (we are unable to provide visa sponsorship for these roles as they do not meet the current minimum salary requirements for sponsorship set by the Home Office. Applications from candidates who have their own legal right to work within the UK must cover the duration of their 3-year training contract and employment)
How the interview process will go
We want you to know what to expect, so here’s the typical process:
• Online application form.
• Online assessments.
• Video interview.
• Virtual assessment centre.
• Final interview in person.
We’ll keep you updated at each stage and share tips to help you prepare. And just so you know: we don’t use AI in any part of our candidate screening process. Every application is reviewed by a real person.
What you get in return
Our benefits are designed to support your life in and outside of work, with options including additional leave, gym membership and employee discounts, alongside pension, health and wellbeing support and a range of protection benefits.
Salary
£29,000 per annum.
Closing date for applications is Sunday 15th November 2026.
Before you go
Wherever you join BDO, you’ll have the chance to learn by doing, work with clients and build your career with people around you to support your development.
The opportunity to build your experience, confidence and career without having to do it alone.
Big responsibility. Personal support.
That’s Beyond the Ordinary.
Apply now.

Job Description:
The opportunity
Leonardo offers a range of Apprenticeships from 2-5yrs. across a variety of STEM and business routes, offering paid training, coupled with on the job learning that enables you to gain practical skills, experience and knowledge that sets up the best start to your career. We offer competitive entry salaries and fully support your academic learning through to qualifications, with salary increases as you progress.

As a Test Engineering Degree Apprentice you will rotate through different projects where you will join specialist teams of engineers and work within our Integrated Project Teams. During your placements you will work with experienced engineers to design and test new and existing products, learning about the engineering lifecycle and using your new skills to solve problems, generate new ideas and support the development of the next generation of EW products.
You will also attend university on a mixture of day and block day release to complete your Embedded Electronics & Systems Design Apprenticeship (ST0151) which includes a BEng (Hons) Electrical and Electronic Engineering. Through your work placements you will record learning activities and evidence to show your competency in set criteria and in your final placement you will complete a project which forms part of your degree.
During your apprenticeship, you will:
• Grow your knowledge of an engineering business and what the role of a Test Engineer is by being part of our Integrated Project Teams.

• Support early careers activities - our apprentices have the opportunity to work as STEM ambassadors in schools, colleges and universities.
Qualifications and entry Criteria
This Apprenticeship assumes the candidate has little professional engineering experience and is NOT suitable for candidates who already have an engineering, software or computing degree.
The starting salary for this role is £23,500
During your Apprenticeship we encourage you to spend at least 3/4 days a week on site to integrate with your team, connect socially and maximise your learning experience.
What we need from you
Qualifications
You must have (as a minimum) the following qualifications:
120 UCAS Points at A'Level to include Maths and Physics, BTEC Extended Diploma or equivalent and 5 GCSE grades 4 - 9 or grades A*- C or equivalent - Mandatory: English, Maths and Science Plus 2 subjects
Security Clearance
At Leonardo, many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations.  As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.
For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV).  As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.
To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years.  In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks.  Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.
For more information and guidance please visit: https://careers.uk.leonardo.com/gb/en/security-and-vetting

Duration: minimum 12 months from October 2027

At Rolls-Royce we are committed to always being a force for progress; powering, protecting and connecting people everywhere.

Enterprise Skills Accelerator is an intensive development programme geared towards future-focused leadership skills.
We know the foundations future business leaders need. And through real-world ‘gigs’ (or placements), group projects, self-driven learning, and access to our amazing leaders, experts and networks, you’ll gain the behavioural, technical and mindset skills that will set you up for success, at pace.

Future-ready skills

Exciting prospects

A network who’ll help you continue to challenge how we work and deliver strategic projects as you move into a future in our open talent marketplace. Gain the skills to transform and perform. Apply now.

Role Summary
The Operations Finance Director provides strategic financial insight, analysis and recommendations on operational and commercial performance across the Group, ensuring financial considerations are embedded in business decisions. The Operations Finance Director acts as a key finance partner to the Commercial and Operations teams, supporting bids, tenders, projects and commercial opportunities through robust financial analysis, modelling and recommendations. Working closely with the Operations Performance and Excellence Team, the role provides financial intelligence and insight to enhance visibility of business performance, emerging risks and opportunities, enabling informed decision-making and supporting the achievement of the Group’s operational and commercial objectives.
Responsibilities
• Provide strategic financial support to the SVP Operations Finance and Tax, acting as a key source of financial data, analysis and business intelligence to support decision-making on operational and commercial performance, key business drivers, risks and opportunities.
• Partner with Operations, Commercial and the Trust and Verify team to develop, interpret and maintain meaningful operational, financial and commercial KPIs and metrics, providing clear visibility of business performance, trends, key drivers and emerging risks and opportunities.
• Partner closely with Commercial leadership throughout the commercial lifecycle, providing financial analysis, insight and challenge across opportunity assessment, tender preparation, Bid Approval Sheets, customer negotiations and contract award decisions.
• Lead financial review and challenge of Bid Approval Sheets and significant commercial proposals, ensuring key assumptions, profitability, cash generation, sensitivities, risks and value drivers are appropriately evaluated to support informed decision-making.
• Provide financial evaluation and decision support for significant projects, contracts, tenders, new country start-ups, rig moves, reactivations and other major operational initiatives, assessing project economics, cost assumptions, expected returns, cash requirements and key financial risks.
• Act as the Operations Finance lead for major operational initiatives, working closely with Regional Finance, Operations and Commercial teams to ensure appropriate financial governance, cost control, AFE compliance and delivery against agreed financial objectives.
• Monitor the financial and operational performance of awarded contracts, projects and major initiatives against the approved business case, identifying material variances, underlying drivers and potential impacts on profitability, EBITDA, cash generation and utilisation.
• Lead post-contract and post-project reviews of significant commercial opportunities and operational initiatives, identifying drivers of success or underperformance, capturing lessons learned and recommending actions to improve future commercial and operational decision-making.
• Develop forward-looking analysis, scenario modelling and sensitivity analysis to support strategic operational and commercial decisions, including fleet deployment, rig reactivations, stacking strategies, new market opportunities, project investment and other significant business decisions.
• Prepare financial analysis, insights and management materials for the SVP Operations Finance and Tax and senior leadership, providing a clear and comprehensive view of operational and commercial performance and supporting executive decision-making.
• Provide independent financial challenge on commercial proposals, project plans and operational strategies, ensuring key assumptions, value drivers, financial risks and potential returns are appropriately assessed, and represent Operations Finance on strategic and cross-functional initiatives where forward-looking financial and commercial analysis is required.
Qualifications and Experience
• Degree in Accounting, Finance or a related discipline preferred.
• Professional accounting qualification (ACCA, CIMA, CPA or equivalent) is desirable.
• Previous experience in a similar role, business partnering, commercial finance, operational finance or project finance, preferably within the energy, offshore or project-based industry.
• Experience supporting commercial tenders, Bid Approval Sheets, contract evaluation, project economics or investment decisions.
• Experience analysing operational and financial performance and translating financial information into clear business insight and recommendations.
• Strong financial modelling and analytical capability, with experience using Excel and ERP/BI tools (e.g. IFS, Power BI) preferred.
• Experience conducting business case reviews, post-contract or post-project analysis, and identifying performance drivers and lessons learned.
• Strong communication and influencing skills, with the ability to work effectively with senior Operations, Commercial and Executive stakeholders.
• Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously while also managing quarterly and annual accounting cycles.
• Ability to take initiative and work on tasks independently or as part of a team.

Working at Citi is far more than just a job. A career with us means joining a team of more than 230,000 dedicated people from around the globe. At Citi, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your career, give back to your community and make a real impact.
Job Overview
Engineer the future of global finance. At Citi, our Tech team doesn’t just support finance – we are helping to redefine it. Every day, $5 trillion crosses through our network. We do business in 180+ countries operating at a scale few can match. From deploying advanced AI to helping shape global markets, we build systems that matter. Help solve real-world challenges that touch millions and get the opportunity to build the future of finance with Citi Tech.
Citi's Equities Technology organization is seeking a Senior Software Engineer – Ultra Low Latency Risk Engine Developer to join the Equities Electronic Execution (Electronic Trading) technology team. This role is focused on the design, development, and delivery of Citi's next-generation low-latency Risk Engine for cash equities and its integration into the broader execution platform — encompassing the Centralised Position Service, Client Connectivity, Market Access layers, and high-throughput market data processing.
The engineer will own critical, latency-sensitive risk-checking components that sit directly in the cash equities trading hot path, ensuring pre-trade and real-time risk controls are enforced with microsecond-level performance while maintaining correctness and resiliency at scale. This is a hands-on, deeply technical role that also carries leadership responsibilities — mentoring engineers, driving architecture decisions, and coordinating delivery across global development centers.
The person will collaborate closely with product development, quantitative research, technology infrastructure, production support, and QA teams, with close alignment to global strategy and cross-regional delivery (APAC, EMEA, NAM).
Responsibilities:
• Partner with multiple management teams to ensure appropriate integration of functions to meet goals as well as identify and define necessary system enhancements to deploy new products and process improvements
• Resolve variety of high impact problems/projects through in-depth evaluation of complex business processes, system processes, and industry standards
• Provide expertise in area and advanced knowledge of applications programming and ensure application design adheres to the overall architecture blueprint
• Utilize advanced knowledge of system flow and develop standards for coding, testing, debugging, and implementation
• Develop comprehensive knowledge of how areas of business, such as architecture and infrastructure, integrate to accomplish business goals
• Provide in-depth analysis with interpretive thinking to define issues and develop innovative solutions
• Serve as advisor or coach to mid-level developers and analysts, allocating work as necessary
• Appropriately assess risk when business decisions are made, demonstrating particular consideration for the firm's reputation and safeguarding Citigroup, its clients and assets, by driving compliance with applicable laws, rules and regulations, adhering to Policy, applying sound ethical judgment regarding personal behavior, conduct and business practices, and escalating, managing and reporting control issues with transparency.
Risk Engine & Core Development
• Design, develop, and maintain the ultra low-latency, in-line Risk Engine responsible for real-time pre-trade risk checks, position limits, and exposure controls across cash equities electronic execution flows.
• Architect and optimize high-performance, lock-minimal, multi-threaded components capable of processing risk decisions in the sub-microsecond to low-microsecond range.
• Integrate risk and position components with Client Connectivity, Market Access layers, and high-throughput market data feed handlers.
• Apply deep expertise in JVM performance tuning, memory management, garbage collection avoidance, and/or native (C++/Rust) performance engineering to eliminate latency outliers ("jitter") in the risk path.
• Perform system-level performance tuning to minimize end-to-end latency and jitter across the risk and execution path.
Recommended Qualifications:
• Proven software engineering experience, with substantial hands-on experience building risk management, position-keeping, or other latency-critical systems for cash equities electronic trading or algorithmic trading platforms at a global investment bank or equivalent financial institution.
• Strong, hands-on technical expertise in Low Latency Java and/or C++ (Rust a plus), including multi-threading, concurrency, lock-free data structures, Java NIO, and JVM/GC performance tuning.
• Hands-on experience with low-latency messaging and IPC frameworks such as Aeron, Solace, or equivalent shared-memory/IPC technologies for building distributed, high-throughput trading systems.
• Demonstrated background in real-time distributed risk management systems for cash equities flow products, including asynchronous, event-driven architectures.
• Practical, hands-on experience with NUMA-aware design, CPU core pinning/affinity and isolation, Linux kernel/OS tuning, and low-latency networking (kernel bypass, RDMA, or specialized NIC tuning) for ultra low-latency, high-throughput systems.
• Strong understanding of automated testing techniques, test-driven development, and quality engineering practices for mission-critical systems.
• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to present and grasp complex technical and risk concepts in a multicultural, cross-regional environment, and to work effectively with globally distributed stakeholders (trading desks, quants, infrastructure, and support teams).
• Working knowledge of regional exchange microstructure and relevant regulatory regimes governing cash equities electronic trading and risk controls.
Education:
• Bachelor’s degree/University degree or equivalent experience
• Master’s degree preferred

As a team
Finance Reinvention Partner (Finance RP) is Accenture's unified UKI Finance practice — around 300 people today, with ambitions to grow significantly — bringing together Consulting, Technology, AI and Operations to be the UKI's Trusted Reinvention Partner for Finance. We pair deep industry expertise with AI at the core and orchestrate our ecosystem partners as the winning formula to drive speed to value for CFOs.
We are building the Future of Finance around three imperatives: finance that is intelligent (real-time decisions, not month-end dashboards), autonomous (process and operations that run themselves — agents, not bots), and evolving (talent, org and commercial model rebuilt around the work). In practice that means delivering the flagship CFO outcomes our leadership is targeting — autonomous finance at scale, the real-time CFO, and cost-to-serve transformation.
You will join our SAP Finance transformation offering, central to one of the practice's headline priorities: capturing the SAP-led Finance transformation opportunity. We lead large-scale, business-led S/4HANA finance transformations, advising and architecting the work, the workforce and the technology, with AI at the core.
As an Associate Manager, you will be
• Delivering S/4HANA-enabled finance transformations from discovery and visioning through business-led design and implementation, owning your part of the work with limited oversight.
• Translating business strategy and finance objectives into S/4HANA-enabled finance process designs across Record to Report, Order to Cash, Procure to Pay and related finance domains.
• Leading fit-to-standard and design decisions in your area, accountable for the choices you make and balancing SAP standard practice with the client's value, control and operating-model needs.
• Applying agentic thinking to finance process design — working out where AI and reasoning-layer tools change how a process should run, not just digitising the current one — and owning that design for the steps you cover.
• Leading smaller workstreams and guiding junior colleagues, reviewing their work and helping them develop.
• Applying structured analysis, business cases and value-led recommendations to complex, ambiguous finance transformation problems.
• Facilitating workshops with senior finance stakeholders to define future-state finance processes, securing design decisions and aligning finance, tax, operations and technology.
• Acting as a bridge between business and technology: working closely with SAP delivery teams while keeping ownership of the finance and business agenda for your workstream.
• Building trusted client relationships and holding responsibility for finance requirements, outcomes and value expectations being met.
• Contributing to business development — helping shape finance transformation propositions, supporting bids, and articulating CFO-relevant value cases.
• Helping grow the practice through assets, points of view and capability-building across S/4HANA-enabled finance transformation.
• Continuing to build new skills as the platform and the finance agenda change.

Hull has the 2nd highest level of flood risk in the UK outside of London. The risk is a combination of multiple sources; tidal, fluvial, surface water, sewer and ground water. There are many organisations with a role in managing the flood risk. These organisations have formed the Living with Water Partnership which aims to create a thriving community in Hull and Haltemprice through working together on flood risk management to become an international exemplar for living in harmony with water.
Over the last 6 years, the flood risk team have been involved in delivering £220 million investment programme into flood infrastructure across the city working alongside partners. Over the next 6 years, the flood risk team will continue to lead and support other risk management authorities, as well as the Living with Water Partnership, to set a global standard for flood resilience. The future of flood risk management will involve using innovative solutions to build resilience through community and educational engagement across schools, partners and stakeholders.
The Flood Officer has an essential role within the Flood Risk Management Team, supporting the Senior Flood Risk Officers Flood Risk Planning Manager, the Development Delivery team and the Living with Water Partnership. This helps ensure that the Council fulfils its duties as a Lead Local Flood Authority as required in the EU (European Union) Floods Directive, the Land Drainage Act 1991, Flood Risk Regulations 2009, Flood and Water Management Act 2010, and the Environment Act 2021.

About the team/job
We are seeking a Bioinformatician with expertise in structural biology, proteomics and integrative/hybrid structure modelling to join the Velankar team at the European Bioinformatics Institute (EMBL-EBI).
The Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe) team develops essential macromolecular structure resources and tools for biologists and other life scientists. As a founding partner of the Worldwide Protein Data Bank, we maintain the global archive of experimentally determined macromolecular structures, the Protein Data Bank (PDB). We also manage the community-led PDBe Knowledge Base (PDBe-KB) and the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database (AFDB), a collaboration with Google DeepMind. The team brings together scientists, software engineers and data engineers to develop tools and services for structure deposition, data integration, advanced search and biological interpretation.
This is an exciting opportunity to develop FAIR infrastructure for structural interactomics and integrative/hybrid modelling. The project will connect experimental proteomics evidence, including crosslinking mass spectrometry (XL-MS), co-fractionation mass spectrometry (CF-MS) and affinity-purification mass spectrometry (AP-MS), with structural restraints, predicted structures, integrative models and molecular interaction data.
Working in close partnership with colleagues in PRIDE and wwPDB, you will help establish the data standards, deposition workflows, validation approaches and access services needed to make these interconnected datasets discoverable, interpretable and reusable. The role is ideal for a scientist who enjoys working across disciplines and wants to make a lasting contribution to open scientific infrastructure.
Your role
You will contribute to the development of standards and infrastructure that connect structural interactomics experiments, proteomics evidence and integrative structure models. You will work at the interface of structural biology, proteomics and scientific software development, applying both biological understanding and technical expertise to improve the interoperability, provenance and reuse of these data.
A central component of the role will be developing practical approaches for representing experimental context and linking evidence across repositories to streamline data deposition. You will contribute to the extension and adoption of established community standards, including those for proteomics metadata and identifications, and develop tools that support the conversion, validation and deposition of standard-compliant data.
You will work closely with international collaborators, community standards organisations, data-resource providers and developers of analysis tools. The resulting infrastructure will enable researchers to move transparently from proteomics evidence and structural restraints to integrative models, molecular interactions and biological annotation.
Your main responsibilities will include:
• Analyse current XL-MS, CF-MS, AP-MS and integrative modelling workflows to define data and metadata requirements.
• Contribute to the extension and adoption of community standards for structural interactomics and integrative modelling data.

Security Clearance

For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV).  As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.

IRC provides a diverse range of services to our clients, including actuarial and internal audit services and those related to Regulatory Compliance. Clients are predominantly from the insurance market but can also include entities in the retail banking, debt and payment sectors.
This role is within the Regulator Compliance team which provides advice and guidance to clients on all aspects of financial services regulation to help them stay compliant and evidence their compliance with the vast web of regulations applicable to the sector.
The team focuses on conduct regulation and guidance as issued by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and regulatory reporting overseen by the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA). The FCA's primary purpose is to protect consumers, protect the integrity of the financial system and to promote competition, in the interests of consumers. It expects regulated entities to put the consumer at the heart of their business. The PRA’s primary objectives are to promote the safety and soundness of regulated entities; and more specific to insurance firms, to ensure policyholders are appropriately protected.

You'll also have the opportunity to develop your technical knowledge, learn from experienced colleagues and build valuable skills within the world of flavour innovation.

• Support the Flavour Creation team with new developments, reformulations and customer projects, ensuring samples are prepared accurately and on time.
• Maintain accurate and confidential formulation records, sample preparation details and laboratory data using internal systems.
• Monitor and maintain raw material stocks, ensuring ingredients are correctly labelled, stored and readily available.
• Work closely with colleagues across Flavour Creation, Production and Sample Bay to support the smooth running of laboratory activities.
• Maintain a clean, safe and organised laboratory environment, ensuring equipment is properly maintained and all activities follow established procedures and safety standards.

• Develop your technical knowledge through hands-on training and collaboration with experienced colleagues.

Essential
• A scientific background, ideally in Chemistry, Food Science, Biology, Biochemistry or a related discipline.
• Exceptional attention to detail, with the ability to work accurately and precisely when following formulations and instructions.
• A careful, methodical approach to completing tasks, with a strong focus on quality and consistency.
• A genuine willingness to learn, listen and develop new technical skills.
• Strong organisational and time management skills, with the ability to manage tasks and priorities effectively.
• A positive, can-do attitude, with a reliable and responsible approach to work.
• Good communication and teamwork skills, with the ability to work collaboratively in a laboratory environment.
Desirable
• A degree in Chemistry, Food Science or a related scientific subject.
• Previous hands-on laboratory experience, including university practical work, placements or internships.
• Experience accurately weighing, measuring or preparing samples in a laboratory environment.
• An interest in food, beverages, ingredients or flavour development.
• Familiarity with laboratory equipment, safety procedures or scientific record-keeping.

As we continue to grow, we want to ensure that Carbery Group continues to be a place where people are supported to develop and feel that they can do their best work. We are committed to driving growth, developing future capability and delivering results through our dedicated teams.

• Move us beyond optimising on installs toward measuring real downstream value and incremental impact.
• Own the measurement stack (attribution, event tracking, value-based signals) and run regular incrementality testing so we can trust what is genuinely driving growth.
• Automate the reporting and account checks that currently eat time, and simplify campaign structures so more effort goes into creative and strategy and less into manually moving budgets between campaigns and markets.

We are seeking a motivated and analytically driven Security Detection & Response Analyst (SDR) to join the GIS Monitoring and Triage team. This role supports cybersecurity operations across threat detection, investigation, response, and continuous service improvement.
The ideal candidate will have security practitioner experience with strong analytical aptitude and foundational technical skills, who contributes to the detection and response lifecycle by supporting investigations and response activities under guidance.
This role focuses on developing the ability to analyse security events, build contextual understanding of threats, and progressively operate with increasing independence across multiple security domains. • Validate alerts and contribute to improving detection fidelity by identifying false positives and providing feedback to enhance detection logic and coverage
• Contribute to the development and refinement of investigation guides, runbooks, and playbooks, while learning to leverage automation, SOAR workflows, and AI-assisted tools to improve efficiency
• Identify gaps in telemetry, monitoring, or processes and escalate improvement opportunities to support continuous enhancement of detection and response capabilities

• Basic experience with log analysis and telemetry interpretation, including familiarity with querying or analyzing data using tools such as SIEM platforms or query languages (KQL, SPL, SQL, or similar)
• Exposure to security platforms and technologies such as SIEM, EDR/XDR, identity systems, or cloud environments
• Foundational understanding of common attacker tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs), with familiarity of frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK
• Analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to follow structured investigation processes and document findings clearly
• Effective communication skills, including the ability to provide clear updates and collaborate with team members during investigations
• Willingness to learn, take direction, and progressively develop independent decision-making capabilities in security operations environments

We are looking for a confident, credible and engaging EHS professional who combines technical expertise with strong leadership and influencing skills.

The Group Risk Team is responsible for identifying, monitoring and managing key risks across all of AXIS’s business and operations. It works closely with multiple stakeholders across AXIS and establishes a view of risk using a mixture of qualitative and quantitative analyses.

What will you do in this role?

You will support the ongoing development and enhancement of the core components of the enterprise risk management framework.

•
You will support the delivery of stress and scenario testing, including coordinating the collection of data and assumptions, performing qualitative and quantitative analysis, and contributing to the preparation of results and supporting materials.

You will support the Internal Model Validation process by bringing together key data, metrics and dashboards to ensure the efficient and timely production of the validation reports.
•
You will support Syndicate risk reporting, including the preparation of regular and ad hoc risk reports.

You will support other members of the Group ERM team in challenging AXIS’s first-line processes relating to key business risks.

You will help maintain the risk management system and its data to ensure they are complete and up to date.

You will participate in project work and deep-dive assessments of topical areas.

Thornton Tomasetti applies engineering and scientific principles to solve the world’s challenges. Our Applied Science practice leverages a unique combination of technologies and expertise to engineer practical solutions to problems of national and international importance.  We apply expertise in solid and fluid dynamics, materials science, acoustics, risk assessments and computational simulation methods to solve complex problems. We perform research, mathematical modeling, software development and design to manage risks to life safety in military platforms and installations, ships and submarines, critical infrastructure, tall buildings, public facilities, industrial and petrochemical plants and automotive and airborne vehicles. Military, government, corporate and academic clients value the validation of Applied Science’s software and the critical insights gained from correlating analysis with testing.
The Role
We have an opportunity for an experienced Seismic Specialist with 8-10 years of experience to join our Applied Science practice in our Warrington office.  Our projects often include structural dynamics, seismic engineering and other specialist subjects and we use a combination of first principles and advanced modelling software to tackle these.
We are looking for an enthusiastic engineer with a good understanding of the skills necessary to provide robust seismic substantiation of a range of nuclear safety-related structures, including their foundations and soil-structure interaction. The role will heavily support Thornton Tomasetti’s strategic development of work within the UK Civil Nuclear sector along with the UK and Australian nuclear submarine programmes.
The ideal candidate will be chartered, or nearing chartership, with a strong grasp of engineering principles, in-depth knowledge of the primary construction materials and a passion for tackling complex engineering challenges. The position involves winning, managing and delivering projects, offering technical guidance to junior team members, and maintaining active engagement with clients.
Thornton Tomasetti prides itself on tackling problems beyond the usual and this results in a unique opportunity to be involved with an ever-changing and diverse range of projects which means our engineers develop a broad range of experience and skills. We will provide training and support to enable you to succeed and apply your skills to these new and exciting problems.
What You’ll Do
•
Responsibilities will include managing and delivering projects, leading complex analysis, and providing oversight and support to junior staff.
•
The role will involve proactively engaging with our clients and preparing project proposals as part of the office business development activity.
•
You will help to develop our specialist structural expertise in areas which, in addition to seismic engineering and SSI, could include blast and explosion response, fatigue and failure assessment and probabilistic analyses.
•
Prior experience in coding and/or numerical simulation (FEA or CFD) would be advantageous.
What You’ll Bring
•
PhD or Master's Degree in civil, structural, or mechanical engineering with at least 8 years of relevant industrial experience.
•
Seismic engineering, dynamic analysis and ideally SSI experie
•
Experience in the Nuclear / Defence sectors is advantageous.
•
ICE / IStructE / IMechE Chartered status, or planning to submit for professional review within the next year.
•
Eligible to obtain UK security clearance.
•
Able to demonstrate experience in solving complex problems and motivated to take the next step in your career by leading challenging projects.
